A claim states that drinking hot water mixed with lemon juice will destroy the coronavirus. This claim is false. Experts have stated that there is no scientific evidence to support this claim, and it has been widely debunked by fact-checkers and health organizations.

Here's what the sources say:
*   AFP reported on March 12, 2020, that claims circulating on Facebook about warm water with lemon preventing coronavirus are false. Experts confirmed there's no proof of its effectiveness, and good hygiene is the best way to stay healthy. [1]
*   Samayam Tamil, on May 26, 2021, addressed the misconception that lemon and hot water can kill the coronavirus, stating it is completely false and lacks scientific evidence. [2]
*   FactCheck.org, on April 2, 2020, debunked a social media post claiming a blend of sodium bicarbonate and lemon juice would "eliminate" the novel coronavirus, emphasizing that there is no specific medicine recommended to prevent or treat COVID-19. [3]
*   VOA, on May 18, 2021, also highlighted that lemon juice will not cure COVID-19, categorizing such claims as "fake news." [4]
*   While lemons are rich in Vitamin C and can boost the immune system, which is generally beneficial for health, this does not mean they can destroy the coronavirus. [5] The World Health Organization's recommendations for preventing COVID-19 include regular handwashing and staying home if unwell. [1]
